profile: CGPA 2.3/4.0. On the University of Ghana scale 2.0–2.49 is a third-class degree; most UK master's ask for a 2:2 (second class lower, about 2.5+). So the best routes are: pre-master's or extended master's courses (UK), programmes that state no minimum grade or no NC (Germany), and graduate certificates or foundation routes (Canada). Your work experience (Carbon Clarity, research, Yamale marketing) strengthens every application. Fully funded scholarships are the hardest with a 2.3, because many set a 2:1 or 3.0+ minimum. The best fully funded routes are leadership fellowships (no grade needed), government awards that weigh experience, and Erasmus Mundus programmes with no stated minimum.

items.title: Pre-Master's Programme (leads to MSc Data Analytics, Project Management, MBA, International Business and more)
items.provider: London Metropolitan University International Study Centre
items.grade: No minimum grade stated: a 3-year degree in a relevant area, each applicant assessed individually.
items.req: Academic IELTS 5.5 (no component below 5.5).
items.start: January 2027 (1 or 2 terms) or May 2027 (1 term)
items.deadlineNote: No fixed deadline published. Apply early for the January 2027 start.
items.funding: Scholarships up to £2,500. London Met also gives eligible Ghanaian students an automatic £5,000 International Bright Futures discount on its courses.
items.fit: The clearest London route for a 2.3: pass the pre-master's and progress to a London Met master's such as Data Analytics or Project Management.

items.title: Extended Masters and Enhanced Extended Masters
items.grade: For applicants who do not meet the standard master's entry requirements; a bachelor's degree is required.
items.req: IELTS 6.5 (Extended) or 6.0 (Enhanced Extended), at least 5.5 in each component.
items.start: Extended: June, July or October. Enhanced Extended: September or February.
items.deadlineNote: No deadline on the overview page; check each course page. February 2027 is the next Enhanced start.
items.funding: UWL international scholarships and bursaries (see the fees and funding page).
items.fit: A preparation stage of 10–14 weeks, then the regular master's. Built for people below the usual grade.

items.title: Postgraduate courses (MBA, International Project Management, International Marketing) with holistic admission
items.grade: Most countries need a 2:2 or equivalent, but ARU London assesses applicants holistically (including relevant work experience), offers a Pre-Masters route, and welcomes mature applicants with relevant experience.
items.req: English proficiency required (see the English requirements page). Check the Ghana entry on the international requirements page.
items.deadlineNote: Intakes listed; confirm course-specific deadlines with admissions.
items.fit: Worth an enquiry: ask whether your work experience can count alongside your 2.3, or go via their Pre-Masters.

items.title: Chevening Scholarships (fully funded UK master's)
items.grade: An undergraduate degree that qualifies you for a UK master's programme (so you need a university offer route, such as those above).
items.req: At least 2,800 hours of work experience after graduating. You must apply to three eligible UK courses.
items.deadlineNote: 2027/28 applications are closed. The 2027/28 round opened in August 2026, so the next round is expected around August 2027: get ready now.
items.fit: Competitive, but your Carbon Clarity work is the kind of leadership story Chevening looks for. Start building essays now.

items.title: MSc International Business (Extended)
items.grade: Explicitly accepts a third class, pass or ordinary degree, or equivalent.
items.req: Academic IELTS 6.0 (no band below 5.5). If below entry, a Graduate Certificate in Business route (50% average to progress).
items.deadlineNote: 2027/28 fees not yet announced; check the course page.
items.fit: Outside London, but one of the few UK master's that names a third-class degree as acceptable.

items.title: Graduate Certificate: Project Management – Environmental (PME)
items.grade: No GPA requirement listed.
items.req: Degree or diploma in environmental studies, planning, science or related. With an unrelated diploma, 2 years of full-time industry-related experience may be considered (CV and references).
items.deadlineNote: Ontario college seats for international students fill early: apply 8–12 months before your start.
items.fit: Matches Carbon Clarity exactly: environmental projects plus project management, with no GPA cut-off.

items.title: Environmental Management and Assessment (1-year graduate certificate)
items.grade: No GPA requirement listed.
items.req: Degree in a listed environmental or science field; with a degree in another field, send a cover letter and CV showing environmental work experience. English proof required.
items.deadlineNote: Check intake status on ontariocolleges.ca and apply early.
items.fit: Your cookstove pilot and field data work are the environmental experience they ask for.

items.title: MBA Foundation (leads to the UCW MBA)
items.grade: Cumulative GPA of 2.33 or better (UCW uses a 4.33 scale). Your 2.3/4.0 is close: check how it converts (e.g., WES) before applying.
items.req: IELTS 6.5 (6.0 writing) or equivalent. Three foundation courses; a B (3.0) average lets you continue into the MBA.
items.deadlineNote: Rolling intakes; see UCW dates and deadlines.
items.fit: A business route for your marketing, sales and venture work, if your GPA converts to 2.33+.

items.title: M.Sc. Sustainability Management and Technologies
items.grade: No NC and no minimum grade listed.
items.req: Bachelor's in economics or a related programme (180 ECTS); missing credits can be covered by relevant work experience. English B2 (e.g., TOEFL iBT 71).
items.deadlineNote: Summer semester: 28 February. Winter semester: 31 August.
items.cost: Service fee €1,200 per semester for non-EU students
items.funding: Low fees; look at DAAD and Deutschlandstipendium later.
items.fit: Sustainability management at a public university with low fees and no grade cut-off.

items.title: M.Sc. Environmental and Resource Management
items.grade: No minimum grade stated on the How to Apply page.
items.req: Relevant bachelor's (natural/environmental sciences, engineering, or socio-economics such as environmental economics). TOEFL iBT 79 or IELTS 6.0. Apply via uni-assist.
items.deadlineNote: Expected date: last published deadline for visa-required applicants was 15 May. Confirm the 2027 date on the BTU page.
items.cost: Public university: semester fee only (check amount)
items.funding: Look at DAAD EPOS and Deutschlandstipendium (competitive).
items.fit: A well-known international environmental master's with no stated grade cut-off.

items.title: MSc Sustainability Management (12 months)
items.grade: No minimum GPA listed; no NC.
items.req: Bachelor's in a related field; IELTS 6 or TOEFL iBT 67 or Duolingo 105; virtual interview.
items.deadlineNote: Deadlines listed: 1 January (winter trimester), 1 May, 1 September.
items.cost: €16,500 per year (or €8,250 with the maximum scholarship)
items.fit: Fast (12 months), English-taught, and the scholarship can halve the cost.

items.title: Postgraduate programmes awarded with University of Roehampton London
items.provider: Berlin School of Business and Innovation (BSBI)
items.grade: No minimum grade stated for Roehampton-awarded programmes: a 3-year bachelor's in a related discipline (or HND/Level 5 diploma with professional experience).
items.req: Proof of English. Decision within about 10 working days.
items.deadlineNote: Rolling admissions.
items.fit: Study in Berlin for a London university degree, with no grade cut-off stated.

items.title: On-campus master's and MBAs
items.provider: IU International University of Applied Sciences
items.grade: IU says: "it's not your grades that count, but what you bring to the table." No minimum grade stated.
items.req: Undergraduate degree with relevant ECTS; some programmes need work experience; IELTS, TOEFL or Cambridge.
items.deadlineNote: Rolling; confirm programme and campus with IU.
items.cost: From about €4,150 per semester plus a one-off €1,500 campus fee (check current offer)
items.fit: Flexible admission and many start dates; good backup option.

items.title: Young Leaders' Committee (15 members)
items.grade: No degree grade required: open to researchers, entrepreneurs, practitioners, graduates and students.
items.req: Aged 18–35 and from an African country. Apply online or through a nomination.
items.deadlineNote: 4 December 2026, 23:59 GMT. Benefits (stipend or travel) aren't stated, so confirm in the application.
items.fit: Your Carbon Clarity work and Ghana carbon market research are exactly what a young climate leaders' committee wants, and it builds your profile for scholarships.

items.title: Africa Youth Climate Fund: grants of $5,000, $10,000 or $20,000
items.provider: Africa Youth Climate Fund (hosted by Green Africa Youth Organization)
items.grade: No grade required. For youth-led organisations and groups in Africa (registered, registration underway, or informal through a fiscal sponsor).
items.req: A youth-led climate or environment initiative with a practical local solution. Check the age rules for 'youth-led' in the call.
items.deadlineNote: Applications opened 10 November 2026 and close 15 January 2027.
items.fit: Could fund Carbon Clarity's next pilot step with the James Town processors, if Carbon Clarity counts as youth-led.

items.title: Obama Foundation Leaders Africa 2027–2028 (8-month hybrid leadership programme)
items.grade: No degree or grade requirement.
items.req: Aged 24–45; citizen/resident of an African country; at least 3 years of relevant experience in your issue area; a leadership role in your changemaking work; English.
items.deadlineNote: Announced deadline 4 December 2026 for the 2027–2028 cohort (the official page may still show last year's timeline: confirm when you apply).
items.funding: Free for participants (stipends and travel not stated)
items.fit: Carbon Clarity (women processors, clean cooking, carbon finance) is a strong changemaking story. A top credential for later scholarship applications.

items.title: Australia Awards Africa: fully funded master's in Australia (2028 intake)
items.grade: The Ghana notice and awards page don't state a minimum degree grade; check the eligibility brochure when the round opens.
items.req: Open to eligible African candidates, including Ghanaians. Priority fields usually include agriculture, energy, environment and climate.
items.deadlineNote: The 2027-intake round closed 30 April 2026. The next round opens 1 February 2027.
items.fit: Government scholarship where work and development impact matter; worth checking the grade rule as soon as it opens.

items.title: Mandela Washington Fellowship (YALI): 6-week leadership institute in the US
items.grade: No degree or grade requirement stated.
items.req: Aged 25–35 (exceptional 21–24 considered), citizen and resident of an eligible Sub-Saharan African country, English, eligible for a J-1 visa.
items.deadlineNote: 2027 applications closed 13 October 2026. The 2027 round opened 22 September 2026, so expect the next round around September 2027.
items.funding: Leadership institute at a US university
items.fit: A flagship programme for young African leaders; your Carbon Clarity work fits the Business & Entrepreneurship or Civic Leadership tracks.

items.title: Erasmus Mundus GrEnFIn: Greening Energy Market and Finance (2027 intake)
items.provider: University of Bologna consortium (with LMU Munich and partners)
items.grade: No minimum grade stated, but academic merit counts for 50 of 100 points, so a 2.3 makes the scholarship a long shot.
items.req: First degree in Mathematics, Physics, Economics, Statistics, IT or Engineering; English B2; a 30-minute online test (maths, statistics, economics, finance) worth 30 points; CV and experience worth 20 points.
items.deadlineNote: 7 January 2027 (from a deadline calendar: confirm on the official GrEnFIn site).
items.cost: Fully funded if you win an Erasmus Mundus scholarship
items.funding: Erasmus Mundus scholarship (tuition, monthly allowance, travel)
items.fit: Energy markets and green finance link straight to carbon markets. Apply only if your degree is in a listed field, and prepare hard for the online test, which can offset your grade.

items.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters catalogue (about 200 fully funded master's)
items.grade: Each programme sets its own rule. Many ask for strong grades (e.g., MESPOM 3.5, MundusMAPP 3.17), so look for programmes with no stated minimum that score work experience.
items.req: Bachelor's degree; English; programme-specific documents. Scholarship deadlines are mostly December to February for September starts.
items.deadlineNote: Mostly December 2026 to February 2027. The daily search will add specific programmes that don't set a minimum grade.
items.fit: Very competitive with a 2.3, but some programmes weigh experience heavily. Your daily search will flag those.

items.title: West Africa Acumen Fellowship (6-month hybrid, Accra and Lagos)
items.grade: No academic prerequisites.
items.req: Minimum 5 years of work experience; social entrepreneur or senior decision-maker working full-time on poverty; West Africa resident (Ghana eligible).
items.deadlineNote: The last published round closed 25 November 2024. Watch for the next call.
items.fit: Ideal once you reach 5 years of experience: Carbon Clarity is exactly the kind of enterprise Acumen backs.

items.title: KAAD scholarship for master's in Germany
items.grade: No minimum grade stated; a relevant first degree and transcripts are assessed.
items.req: Catholic, Christian or engaged in interreligious dialogue; recommendation from the KAAD partner committee in Ghana; German A2/B1 on arrival and B2 for studies; motivation letter, study plan, two references.
items.deadlineNote: Rounds close 15 January and 15 June. Contact the KAAD partner committee in Ghana well before.
items.funding: About €992/month (master's), tuition where charged, insurance, travel, German course
items.fit: A strong match if you're a practising Christian: KAAD looks at commitment and development impact, not just grades. Pair it with a no-NC German master's such as THI or BTU.

items.title: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship (JJ/WBGSP)
items.provider: World Bank and Government of Japan
items.grade: No GPA rule stated on the programme page; partner programmes do their own selection.
items.req: 3+ years of paid, full-time, development-related work since your bachelor's (within the last 6 years), currently in such a job, and unconditional admission to a partner programme. Check Ghana is on the eligible-country list.
items.deadlineNote: Window 1: 18 January to 26 February 2027. Window 2: 29 March to 21 May 2027.
items.funding: Tuition, flights + US$600 travel allowance, monthly allowance, insurance
items.fit: Possible if your Carbon Clarity and research work count as 3 years of paid development work. You need a partner programme admission first.

items.region: Africa, Canada, UK, Europe and more
items.title: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program (master's)
items.grade: Set by each partner university (often competitive).
items.req: Talented, service-oriented young Africans from under-represented backgrounds; apply through each partner university.
items.deadlineNote: Each university has its own deadline (many September to January). See 'Where to apply' on the foundation's site.
items.fit: Your community work with James Town processors fits the 'service-oriented' focus; target partner universities whose grade rules you meet.

items.title: Rotary Peace Fellowship: fully funded master's (2028–29 intake)
items.city: Bradford (UK), Uppsala, Duke/UNC, ICU Tokyo, Queensland
items.grade: No GPA or grade minimum stated; Rotary looks for 'academically strong' candidates with a record of achievement in peace or development work.
items.req: Bachelor's degree; at least three years of full-time relevant experience in peace or development work; at least 3 years since your last degree; proficient in English; not currently enrolled. Cannot study at a Peace Center in your home country.
items.deadlineNote: Official page: the 2027-28 application is closed; the 2028-29 application 'will be available online in February 2027'. Deadline not yet published.
items.funding: Tuition and fees, room and board, round-trip travel, internship and field-study expenses (15–24 month master's)
items.fit: Possible: frame Carbon Clarity's work with James Town women processors (livelihoods, clean air, climate) as development work. University of Bradford's Peace Studies and International Development is in the UK. Rotary clubs in Accra can advise on endorsement.

items.title: Community Solutions Program 2027 (3–4 month US professional exchange for community leaders)
items.grade: No degree or grade requirement in the official eligibility list.
items.req: Ghanaian citizen living and working in Ghana; aged 27–39 at the time of application; at least five years of experience working on community issues with measurable benefits to local communities; high level of spoken and written English; eligible for a J-1 visa; return home for at least two years. Focus: regional economic growth and community prosperity (sectors include business and entrepreneurship, technology and innovation).
items.start: August 2027 (orientation 2–5 Aug, practicum 9 Aug–29 Oct, workshop 1–4 Nov 2027, subject to confirmation)
items.deadlineNote: Official IREX application instructions: Tuesday 24 November 2026, 11:59 p.m. Eastern (Washington, D.C.) time, which is 04:59 on 25 November in Accra. Apply online only at csp.irex.org. Finalists notified 25 February 2027.
items.funding: J-1 visa support, round-trip travel, monthly allowance for housing, meals and living expenses, accident and sickness coverage.
items.fit: Closed: the deadline (24 November 2026, 11:59 p.m. US Eastern) has passed. Watch IREX for the 2028 cycle (usually opens around October).

items.title: Jim Leech Mastercard Foundation Fellowship on Entrepreneurship (2027 cohort, 8 months, virtual)
items.provider: Queen's University Dunin-Deshpande Innovation Centre with the Mastercard Foundation
items.grade: No grade requirement stated.
items.req: For 'African students and recent graduates' of any post-secondary institution in Africa, any discipline. 'Recent graduate' is not defined, so email jimleechfellowship@queensu.ca to confirm you qualify before investing much time. At least 10 hours a week; English. Existing ventures or new ideas both welcome.
items.start: January 2027 (Explore Jan–Feb, Ignite Mar–Apr, Launch and Fellowship May–Aug, graduation August)
items.deadlineNote: The official page says 'Apply By December 1, 2026' (it also shows a 'notify me when applications launch' form, so confirm the form is accepting entries). Results late December.
items.funding: Up to 60 Fellows get a stipend (the page says $500 CAD in one place and USD 350 in another) and can pitch for prizes of up to $15,000 CAD and access seed funding.
items.fit: Carbon Clarity is a real venture with a clear story (clean ovens, women processors, carbon credits), and a Canadian university and Mastercard Foundation link helps later Canada and MCF scholarship applications. Main risk: you may not count as a 'recent graduate'.

items.title: Green RISE West Africa Fellowship 2027 (Acumen Academy, for green/climate entrepreneurs)
items.grade: No degree or grade requirement stated.
items.req: Official page: applicants must be based in Nigeria, Ghana, Liberia, Sierra Leone or The Gambia; a minimum of 5 years of professional experience; and a minimum of 5 full-time employees. Check whether Carbon Clarity/your role meets the 5-years and 5-employees rules before applying.
items.deadlineNote: Official page: 'Applications close on 22 December, 2026.'
items.funding: Fully funded leadership programme (no stipend stated)
items.fit: Strong topical match (clean ovens, women processors, carbon) but the 5-years-experience and 5-employee thresholds may rule you out; worth it only if you meet both.

excluded.why: Ghana's nomination rules for master's ask for a Second Class Upper degree.

excluded.name: Commonwealth Scholarships (UK)
excluded.why: Require at least an upper second-class (2:1) degree.

excluded.name: MESPOM (Erasmus Mundus)
excluded.why: Asks for a GPA of 3.5 or above.

excluded.name: MundusMAPP (Erasmus Mundus)
excluded.why: Asks for a GPA of at least 3.17/4.0.

excluded.name: Yale Emerging Climate Leaders Fellowship
excluded.why: Not a grade issue: the 2027 round closed 30 July 2026 and it expects about 5 years of experience. Worth a try for 2028.

excluded.name: Ireland Fellows Programme (Ghana)
excluded.why: Needs a 3.0/4.0 GPA (2:1); a 2:2 only with substantial relevant work experience. A 2.3 / third class does not meet the rule. Checked 2026-11-21.

excluded.name: Türkiye Bursları (Turkish Government master's scholarship)
excluded.why: Official minimum for master's is 75% academic achievement (and under age 30). A 2.3/4.0 CGPA falls below that.

excluded.name: DAAD EPOS scholarships
excluded.why: Requires at least Second Class Upper (2:1) bachelor's (DAAD Ghana official page).

excluded.name: DENSYS 2.0 (Erasmus Mundus, Decentralised Smart Energy Systems)
excluded.why: Official application page: requirements 'may be assessed as not fulfilled if' the 'average grade (CGPA or equivalent) is lower than 3.0 / 4.0', and the degree must be a science/engineering bachelor's with applied thermodynamics, heat transfer and fluid mechanics. Marks count for up to 45 of 100 points. 2027 call closes 27 January 2027, 18:00 Paris time; a 2.3 CGPA is below the stated bar.

excluded.name: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS, Korea)
excluded.why: 2026 GKS-G guidelines require a CGPA of at least 2.64/4.0 (or 80%/top 20% of class); 2.3/4.0 falls below unless you can document a top-20% rank.

funders.name: Chevening (UK Government)
funders.what: Fully funded 1-year master's: tuition, living allowance, flights.
funders.rule: Degree that qualifies you for a UK master's (a pre-master's or extended route can give you that) and 2,800 hours of work after graduating. No fixed degree class.
funders.when: Opens around August, closes around October.

funders.name: KAAD (Catholic Academic Exchange Service, Germany)
funders.what: Monthly stipend (about €992 for master's), tuition where charged, insurance, travel, German course.
funders.rule: Catholic, Christian or active in interreligious dialogue; relevant first degree; recommendation from the KAAD partner committee in Ghana. No minimum grade stated. German B2 needed for study.
funders.when: Two rounds a year: 15 January and 15 June.

funders.name: Joint Japan/World Bank Graduate Scholarship (JJ/WBGSP)
funders.rule: 3+ years of paid development work after your bachelor's and a current development job; unconditional admission to a partner programme first. No GPA rule stated, but the partner programmes are selective. Check Ghana is on the eligible-country list.
funders.when: 2027 windows: 18 Jan–26 Feb and 29 Mar–21 May.

funders.name: Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program
funders.where: Partner universities in Africa, North America, Europe and the Middle East
funders.what: Full scholarships for talented young Africans from under-represented backgrounds.
funders.rule: Apply through each partner university; each sets its own grades and deadlines (often high).
funders.when: Varies by university; many open September to January.

funders.name: Australia Awards Africa (Australian Government)
funders.rule: Ghanaians are eligible. The minimum grade isn't stated on the pages checked: check the brochure when the round opens.

funders.name: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EU)
funders.rule: Each programme sets its own bar. Many want 3.0–3.5 GPA; look for ones with no stated minimum that score experience or tests.

funders.name: Commonwealth Scholarships (UK)
funders.rule: Requires at least an upper second-class (2:1) degree.

funders.name: Stipendium Hungaricum (Hungary)
funders.rule: Ghana's Scholarships Secretariat asks for a Second Class Upper for master's.

funders.name: Swedish Institute Scholarships for Global Professionals
funders.what: Tuition, SEK 12,000 a month, travel grant.
funders.rule: Ghana is not on the 2027 list of eligible citizenships.
funders.when: University applications by 15 January; SI application 8–24 February 2027.

funders.name: DAAD Leadership for Africa (West and Central Africa)
funders.rule: Only for Cameroon, Senegal and Togo (citizens or refugees there).

funders.name: OPEC Fund Scholarship
funders.rule: Paused: "restructuring its scholarship program and is not accepting applications."

funders.name: Rotary Peace Fellowships (The Rotary Foundation)
funders.what: Up to 50 fully funded master's fellowships a year in peace and development.
funders.rule: Bachelor's + 3 years full-time peace or development experience; no GPA minimum stated.

funders.name: Ireland Fellows Programme – Africa (Irish Aid)
funders.what: Fully funded one-year master's in Ireland for early-to-mid-career professionals from listed African countries (Ghana is eligible).
funders.rule: Official page: bachelor's 'with a minimum grade point average of 3.0 (4.0 scale)', i.e. first class or second class upper; 'a second class honour Grade 2 may be accepted if the applicant has substantial directly relevant work experience'. A third class / 2.3 is below even that exception. Also 2+ years' relevant work and degree awarded 2015 or later.
funders.when: 2027-28 call closed (reported deadline 26 July 2026); next call not yet announced.

funders.name: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships, Turkish Government)
funders.what: Fully funded master's in Türkiye with university placement, monthly stipend, tuition, health insurance, accommodation, a Turkish language course and a one-off flight ticket. Open to most nationalities, including Ghanaians.
funders.rule: Official criteria: minimum academic achievement 'For graduate candidates: 75%' and, for master's programmes, 'being under the age of 30'. A 2.3/4.0 CGPA is below the 75% bar, so not suitable unless your transcript converts to 75%+.
funders.when: General application period 10 January – 20 February (official calendar; the year isn't stated, so the 2027 call is expected in that window).

funders.name: Brot für die Welt (Bread for the World) scholarships
funders.where: Postgraduate study in your home country/region (Leadership for Change in the Global South); other strands in Germany
funders.what: Protestant church development agency. Supports 'young, socially committed leaders in the Global South who already have some professional experience' with financial support, mentoring and a study-accompanying programme for a postgraduate degree (e.g. master's).
funders.rule: Official page: 'only our partner organisations process and approve scholarship applications' — you need a nomination via a Brot für die Welt partner (e.g. a church or NGO partner in Ghana). No minimum grade, nationality list or amounts stated publicly.
funders.when: No public deadline; enquire via a partner organisation or stipendien@brot-fuer-die-welt.de.

funders.name: DAAD EPOS (Development-Related Postgraduate Courses, Germany)
funders.what: Fully funded master's in development-related courses at German universities.
funders.rule: DAAD Ghana: 'Applicants must have obtained a Bachelor's Degree graded at least Second Class (Upper Division)' plus two years' professional experience; degree within the last six years. A 2.3 CGPA doesn't meet this.
funders.when: Deadlines set by each university (mostly Aug–Oct).

funders.name: Mauritius–Africa Scholarship Scheme (Government of Mauritius)
funders.what: Scholarships for full-time, on-campus undergraduate and postgraduate study (Master's, MPhil, PhD) at public higher-education institutions in Mauritius; the Ghana Scholarships Authority says financial components (tuition, stipend, airfare) follow the scheme's terms.
funders.rule: Ghana Scholarships Authority notice: 'Must be a Ghanaian citizen resident in Ghana' and 'Must satisfy the minimum admission requirements of the chosen Mauritian public HEI' (no minimum class of degree stated); postgraduate applicants submit an abridged research plan; MPhil/PhD under 40 on 1 January 2027. Check each university's master's entry rule for a third class.
funders.when: The 2026/27 round closed 5 March 2026. The next round isn't published; going by last year, a call is expected around February 2027 (expected, not confirmed).

funders.name: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS, Korean Government / NIIED)
funders.what: Fully funded graduate scholarship (tuition, stipend, airfare, Korean language year). Ghana has an Embassy Track quota (7 in 2026) and University Track R-GKS places.
funders.rule: 2026 guidelines: CGPA 'must be equal to or above 2.64/4.0' (or 80%+ on a 100-point scale, or 'ranked in the top 20% of one's class'). A 2.3/4.0 is below this unless your transcript shows top-20% class rank.
funders.when: 2026 embassy-track applications ran in February 2026; the 2027 round is expected around February 2027 (expected, not confirmed).
